samples.summary: Document-mutating list/task commands carry no read-only self-check; the read-only gate lives only in callers
samples.evidence: `setTaskChecked` (list-commands.ts:332-350) and the list toggles/indent commands (lines 293-324) dispatch `view.dispatch(view.state.update({changes…}))` unconditionally. This change broadens what they rewrite (blockquoted lines now parse as list/task lines instead of being skipped by the removed `p.quoted` bail-out in `replacePrefixes`), so more source text is reachable through them. Unlike the sibling handler `noteCheckboxInput` (checkbox-input.ts:28-34), which refuses to write when `view.state.readOnly` or `!view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`, these functions rely entirely on the caller: editor.ts:258 passes `onToggleTask: undefined` for a read-only mount, and preview.ts:282 then never attaches `onTaskClick`; the toolbar buttons are hidden by `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:252). Note that editor.ts:413 sets only `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)`, which does NOT block programmatic dispatch, and editor.ts:581-585 exposes `toggleBulletList/indentList/outdentList` on the returned API even for a read-only mount — so any future caller (or a UI state slip) that invokes one of these on a viewer-role share-link mount would write to the synced doc with no in-function refusal. Server-side, `YorkieAuthController` would deny a viewer's `rw` attach (line 200), but only when `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`; in shadow mode (lines 97-105) the write is allowed through. I could not construct a reachable bypass on this branch, hence medium confidence and defense-in-depth severity: adding the same `state.readOnly / EditorView.editable` guard the checkbox input already has would make the gate local to the write.
